question: GQ-004
subject: the flagged item resolved, and a rule that existed only as an act

flagged_item_resolved.creator: Uploaded for the author by Harsh Kapoor, SACW.NET
flagged_item_resolved.verdict: The user-upload collection, no institutional sponsor, no licence URL, a 2025 book by a living author. Its "Public Domain License" tag is free text. Still in the list and still flagged — excluding it on those grounds would be a copyright judgement, but the EVIDENCE grade now says exactly what it is.

the_gutenberg_finding.observed: 3 of 5 sampled items came from collection: gutenberg
the_gutenberg_finding.why_title_dedup_missed_them: IA titles differ slightly from Gutenberg's — "Ermeline a ballad" against "Ermeline: A Ballad" — so normalised titles do not match even though the works are identical.
the_gutenberg_finding.the_original_contract: want-list.json records "gutenberg_mirrors_excluded: 1" — a COUNT, not a rule. The exclusion was an act someone performed, not something a later generator could inherit. That is why mine reproduced a solved problem.

after_the_fix.note: 309 excluded against 25 visible in the output: most mirrors were already dropped by title dedup before reaching the identifier check. The jurisdiction-scoped group vanished entirely — all 25 "Public domain in the USA." items were Gutenberg mirrors.

lesson: A constraint recorded as its result cannot be re-applied. "We excluded 1 mirror" is a fact about the past; "exclude identifiers ending in gut" is a rule. The first is what the artifact carried.
